trial_court: Family Court at Secunderabad, O.S. No. 39 of 2000
case_name: Smt. P. Kalavathi vs Smt. P. Lakshmi And Anr
facts_of_case: The plaintiff's husband died intestate, leaving behind a residential house. The defendants trespassed into the property claiming to be the second wife. The plaintiffs filed a suit for declaration and recovery of possession.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage is void ab initio if it is performed during the subsistence of a valid marriage.
legal_principles.held: It was submitted that during the subsistence of the said valid marriage, late P. Venkat Swamy could not have performed a second marriage and, therefore, any alleged marriage set up by defendant No.1 is void ab initio under Sections 5(1) and 11 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: A person who enters into possession of property without any lawful right, title, or interest is not entitled to retain it.
legal_principles.held: It was urged that the defendant No.1 entered into possession of the suit schedule property only after the death of late P. Venkat Swamy, without any lawful right, title, or interest, and that the plaintiffs, being the lawful heirs, were entitled to seek recovery of possession.

outcome.result: Appeal Suit decreed in favour of the respondents
outcome.final_order: The trial court's judgment and decree dated 04.06.2002 were upheld, declaring the suit filed by the plaintiffs against the defendants for declaration and recovery of possession.
